nodes.description: Constant uint public GRACE_PERIOD = 14 days used to bound staleness of queued transactions.
Constant uint public MINIMUM_DELAY = 2 days, lower bound for delay.
Constant uint public MAXIMUM_DELAY = 30 days, upper bound for delay.
Address public admin, the privileged account allowed to queue, cancel and execute transactions.
Address public pendingAdmin, the candidate admin that must accept the role.
Uint public delay, the minimum waiting period before a queued transaction can execute.
Mapping(bytes32 => bool) public queuedTransactions tracking which transaction hashes have been queued.
Public function setDelay(uint delay_) that can only be invoked by the Timelock itself and updates the delay state variable.
Public function acceptAdmin() letting the pendingAdmin become the new admin and clearing pendingAdmin.
Public function setPendingAdmin(address pendingAdmin_) restricted to the Timelock itself.
Public function queueTransaction(...) restricted to admin, computing a txHash and marking it queued.
Public function cancelTransaction(...) restricted to admin, unsetting the queued flag for a txHash.
Public payable function executeTransaction(...) restricted to admin that performs an arbitrary external call after timelock checks.
Internal view function getBlockTimestamp() returning block.timestamp.
Caller-supplied msg.sender used for administrative access-control checks.
Miner-influenceable block.timestamp returned by getBlockTimestamp and used in timelock checks.
Low-level external call target.call.value(value)(callData) in executeTransaction, an arbitrary call to an attacker/queue-controlled address.
Parameter delay_ of setDelay used as the new delay value.
Parameter pendingAdmin_ of setPendingAdmin written into pendingAdmin.
Parameter target of queueTransaction hashed into txHash.
Parameter eta of queueTransaction compared with getBlockTimestamp().add(delay).
Parameter target of executeTransaction, address invoked by the external call.
Parameter value of executeTransaction, wei forwarded to the external call.
Parameter signature of executeTransaction, selector prefix for callData.
Parameter data of executeTransaction, appended into callData.
Parameter eta of executeTransaction used in timelock and grace-period checks.
Local bytes callData built in executeTransaction and passed to the external call.
Local bool success returned from the external call and checked with require.

edges.reason: msg.sender is compared against address(this) in setDelay, so the caller identity gates the state change.
acceptAdmin requires msg.sender == pendingAdmin and then assigns admin = msg.sender.
setPendingAdmin requires msg.sender == address(this) before writing pendingAdmin.
queueTransaction requires msg.sender == admin before queueing a transaction.
cancelTransaction requires msg.sender == admin before unsetting the queued flag.
executeTransaction requires msg.sender == admin before performing the arbitrary external call.
block.timestamp is read by getBlockTimestamp, a timestamp dependency.
eta >= getBlockTimestamp().add(delay) makes queueTransaction depend on miner-influenceable time.
executeTransaction compares getBlockTimestamp() against eta and eta + GRACE_PERIOD.
target parameter flows into the low-level external call as the callee address.
value parameter flows into the external call as the forwarded ether amount.
signature is hashed into a bytes4 selector that is prepended to callData.
data parameter is assigned or abi.encodePacked into callData.
callData is the payload supplied to target.call.value(value).
setDelay writes the delay state variable.
acceptAdmin writes the admin state variable.
acceptAdmin resets pendingAdmin to address(0).
setPendingAdmin writes the pendingAdmin state variable.
queueTransaction sets queuedTransactions[txHash] = true.
cancelTransaction sets queuedTransactions[txHash] = false.
executeTransaction reads and then clears queuedTransactions[txHash].
admin state variable is read as the authorization gate in queueTransaction.
admin state variable is read as the authorization gate in cancelTransaction.
admin state variable is read as the authorization gate in executeTransaction.
executeTransaction unconditionally reaches the external low-level call after only clearing the queued flag.
The external call can invoke back into executeTransaction (or other Timelock entry points) via a malicious target contract.

normalization_plan.reason: delay_ is a parameter of setDelay and only exists within that function's data flow.
pendingAdmin_ is a parameter of setPendingAdmin assigned directly to the pendingAdmin state variable.
target is a queueTransaction parameter hashed into txHash within the function.
eta is a queueTransaction parameter used only in the timelock require within the function.
exec_target is an executeTransaction parameter consumed by the external call in that function.
exec_value is an executeTransaction parameter consumed by the external call in that function.
exec_signature is an executeTransaction parameter used to build callData inside that function.
exec_data is an executeTransaction parameter used to build callData inside that function.
exec_eta is an executeTransaction parameter used only in timelock checks inside that function.
callData is a local variable that flows directly into the unsafe external call.
success is a local variable holding the result of the unsafe external call.
